{1–5} At that time the Persians and the Romans were among the strongest states on earth, and they waged wars and battles against each other of the kind that take place between evenly matched powers. [The believers] loved the victory and dominance of the Romans over the Persians, while the polytheists, because they shared polytheism with the Persians, loved the dominance of the Persians over the Romans. The polytheists of Mecca rejoiced at this, and the Muslims grieved. **Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on Surah 30, verses 11–16:**

﴿11–13﴾ He, the Exalted, informs us that He alone originates the creatures and then brings them back. Then to Him they will be returned after their restoration, so that He may recompense them for their deeds. For this reason He mentioned the recompense of the people of evil and then the recompense of the people of good, saying: ﴿And on the day the Hour is established﴾, when people stand before the Lord of the worlds, and [they see] the Resurrection with their own eyes, ﴿the criminals will be struck dumb﴾; that is, they will despair of every good. This is because they had sent forward for that day nothing but crimes, which are sins of disbelief, polytheism and disobedience. When they had sent forward the causes of punishment without mixing them with any cause of reward, they despaired, were struck dumb, and were left bankrupt. What they used to fabricate about the benefit of their associates, and that these would intercede for them, went astray from them. For this reason He said: ﴿And there will not be for them any intercessors from among their associates﴾, whom they worshipped alongside Allah, ﴿and they will be, in regard to their associates, disbelievers﴾. The polytheists will disown those whom they associated with Allah, and the deities that were worshipped will disown them and say: "We disown You; they never used to worship us." They will be humiliated and will withdraw far away.

﴿14–16﴾ On that day the people of good and the people of evil will separate, just as their deeds separated them in the world. ﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds﴾, who believed in their hearts and confirmed that belief through righteous deeds, ﴿they will be in a garden﴾, containing every kind of plant and all kinds of desirable things, ﴿delighted﴾; that is, they will be gladdened and blessed with delicious foods and drinks, beautiful companions of the Paradise (houris), servants, youths, enchanting voices, moving melodies, wondrous sights, pleasant fragrances, joy, happiness, pleasure and delight, of a kind that no one can describe. ﴿As for those who disbelieved﴾, who denied His blessings and met them with disbelief, ﴿and denied Our signs﴾, which Our messengers brought to them, ﴿they will be in the punishment, brought forth﴾ into it, with Hell encompassing them from all their directions, the painful punishment reaching their hearts, scalding water roasting their faces and cutting their intestines. So where is the difference between the two groups? And where is the equality between those who were blessed and those who were punished?

{17-18} This is information about His being exalted above all imperfection and deficiency, and holy beyond having any of creation resemble Him. It is also a command to the servants to glorify Him in the evening and the morning, at the time of 'ashi (the late afternoon), and at the time of zuhr (midday). These five times are the times of the five daily prayers. God commanded His servants to glorify and praise Him during them. This includes what is obligatory (wajib), such as the five prayers that contain it, and what is recommended (mustahabb), such as the remembrances of morning and evening, the remembrances after the prayers, and the supererogatory prayers (nawafil) associated with them. The reason is that these times, which God chose for the obligatory prayers, are the best times. So glorifying Him, praising Him, and worshipping Him during them is better than at other times. Indeed, worship is included even if it does not contain the words "Glory be to God," because sincerity (ikhlas) in it is a declaration of God's transcendence through action, that He has no partner in worship, and that no creature deserves what is due to Him of sincere devotion and turning back to Him.

{19} ﴿He brings the living out of the dead﴾: as He brings plants out of dry earth, the ear of grain out of the seed, the tree out of the pit, the chick out of the egg, and the believer out of the disbeliever... and the like. ﴿And brings the dead out of the living﴾: the reverse of what was mentioned. ﴿And revives the earth after its death﴾: He sends down rain upon it while it is dead and lifeless. When water is sent down upon it, it stirs, swells, and grows every beautiful kind of plant. ﴿And thus you will be brought out﴾: from your graves.

This is a decisive proof and a clear demonstration that the One who revived the earth after its death will revive the dead. There is no difference in the view of reason between the two matters, and there is no reason to deem either one unlikely when the other is witnessed.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 30, verses 28–29:

{28} This is a parable that God struck for the ugliness and repulsiveness of shirk (associating partners with God). It is a parable drawn from yourselves, requiring no effort of unloading and travelling or driving camels. {Do you have, from among what your right hands possess, partners in what We have provided for you?}; that is: Does any of your slaves, male or female, who are owned, share with you in your provision, such that you and they are equal in it? {Do you fear them as you fear one another?}; that is: as free partners who are truly equal, whose share might be feared to be taken, or whose individual portion of everything might be disputed? Not so! None of what your right hands possess is a partner to you in what God has provided you. Moreover, you did not create them or provide for them, and they too are owned, just like you. So how can you be content to make for God a partner from among His creation, and place it in His station and as His equal in worship, while you are not content for your slaves to be equal to you? This is among the most wondrous of things, and among the clearest proofs of the foolishness of whoever takes a partner with God, and that what he has taken is false and perishing, having no equality with God and no share of worship at all. {Thus do We detail the signs}: by clarifying them through their examples {for a people who use their reason}: who understand the realities and recognize them. As for one who does not use reason, even if the signs were detailed for him and the proofs made clear to him, he would have no intellect by which to perceive what has become evident, nor any understanding by which to grasp what has been made plain. The people of intellect and discernment are the ones to whom speech is addressed and to whom the address is directed.

{29} Since it is known from this parable that whoever takes, besides God, a partner whom he worships and upon whom he relies in his affairs, has nothing of the truth with him, what then compelled them to proceed with a matter that is false, whose falsehood has been made clear and whose proof has become manifest? What compelled them to this was following their desires. Hence He said: {Rather, those who did wrong followed their desires without knowledge}: their deficient souls were inclined toward what the manifest deficiency in them made their desire attach to, a matter which reason decisively judges to be corrupt and which the natural disposition (fitrah) rejects, without any knowledge guiding them to it or any proof leading them to it. {So who can guide those whom God has led astray?}; that is: do not wonder at their not being guided, for God has led them astray because of their wrongdoing, and there is no way to guide one whom God has led astray, since no one opposes God or contends with Him in His dominion. {And they have no helpers}: who would help them when the word of punishment is due against them and their ties and means are cut off.

{30} God commands sincere devotion to Him in all circumstances and the establishment of His religion, saying: {So set your face}; that is, direct and turn it {toward the religion}, which is Islam, faith (iman), and excellence (ihsan). This means turning your heart, intention, and body to establishing the outward rites of the religion, such as prayer, zakat, fasting, pilgrimage, and the like, and its inward rites, such as love, fear, hope, and turning back to God (inabah), along with excellence in both the outward and inward rites, by worshipping God as if you see Him; and if you do not see Him, then indeed He sees you.

God specified the "setting of the face" because the turning of the face follows the turning of the heart, and bodily striving follows from both matters. For this reason He said: {hanifan}; that is, turning toward God in this, turning away from anything else. This command that We have addressed to you is {the nature (fitrah) of God upon which He created mankind}: He placed in their minds the recognition of its goodness and the reprehensibility of anything else. Indeed, God has placed in the hearts of all creation an inclination toward all the outward and inward provisions of the Law, placing in their hearts love of the truth and preference for the truth, and this is the reality of the fitrah. {31} {Turning back to Him (munibina ilayhi) and fear Him}: This is an explanation of setting the face toward the religion, for inabah is the turning of the heart and the drawing of its motives toward the pleasure of God, and this necessarily entails the body's acting in accordance with what is in the heart. This encompasses both outward and inward acts of worship, and this is not complete except by abandoning the outward and inward sins; therefore He said: {and fear Him}, which includes performing what is commanded and abandoning what is forbidden. He specified prayer among the commanded acts because it calls to turning back and to piety, as in His words: {And establish prayer; indeed, prayer forbids immorality and wrongdoing}, which is its assistance in piety. {38} That is: give the relative close to you—according to his closeness and need—his right, which the Lawgiver has made obligatory or urged, from obligatory maintenance, charity, gifts, kindness, greeting, honoring, pardoning his slip, and overlooking his lapse. If the Face of God is not intended by it, it is not good for the giver, even if it is good and beneficial for the recipient, as He, the Exalted, said: {There is no good in much of their secret talk, except for one who enjoins charity, or what is right, or reconciliation among people}. Its implication is that these exceptions are good because of their beneficial effect on others; but whoever does that seeking the pleasure of God, We will give him a great reward. His saying {And those}: those who performed these deeds and others for the Face of God, {they are the successful}: those who win God's reward and are saved from His punishment.

{39} When He mentioned the deed directed toward His Face through expenditures, He mentioned the deed directed toward a worldly aim, saying: {And what you give in usury (riba) so that it may increase within the wealth of people}; that is, what you give from your wealth beyond your needs, your intention being that it should increase (yarbu), i.e., grow your wealth, by giving it to someone you hope will repay you with more than it. This deed's reward does not increase with God, because the condition of sincerity, which is the requirement, is absent.
Similar to this is the deed intended to increase standing and to gain display (riya') before people; all of this does not increase with God. {And what you give in zakat}; that is, wealth that purifies you from base character traits, purifies your wealth from stinginess with it, and increases the relief of the recipient's need; {desiring}: by it {the Face of God, those are the ones who receive multiplied (al-mudifun)}; that is, those for whom the reward is multiplied, whose expenditures grow with God, and God makes them grow for them until they become abundant. Thus the mere giving of wealth is not good in itself unless it is in this state, namely that it is done in a manner by which the giver purifies himself.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 30, verse 41:

{41} That is: corruption became apparent {in the land and the sea}; that is, the corruption of their livelihoods and their diminishment, the befalling of calamities upon them, and in their own selves, through diseases, plague, and other such things. This is due to what their hands have committed of corrupt deeds that by their very nature cause corruption. This is what is mentioned. {So that He may let them taste part of what they have done}; that is, so that they may know that He is the one who recompenses deeds, so He hastened for them a sample of the recompense of their deeds in this world. {Perhaps they may return}: from their deeds that produced in them the corruption they produced, so their conditions would be set right and their affairs would be made straight. Glory be to Him who bestows favor through His trials and shows kindness through His punishment. Otherwise, had He made them taste all that they had earned, He would not have left upon its surface a single creature.

{42} The command to travel through the land includes travel with the body and travel in the heart, for reflection and contemplation on the outcomes of those who came before. {Most of them were polytheists}: you will find that their end was the worst of ends and their final state the worst of states: a punishment that uprooted them, censure, and a curse from the creation of God that follows them, and a continuous disgrace. So beware of doing their deeds, lest you follow their path, for the justice and wisdom of God are the same in every time and every place.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 30, verses 43–45:

{43} That is: turn your heart toward it and direct your face to it, and strive with your body to establish the upright, straight religion. Carry out His commands and prohibitions with earnestness and diligence, fulfil its outward and inward duties, and hasten to do so in your time, your life and your youth, {before there comes a Day which no one can avert from Allah}: this is the Day of Resurrection, which, once it comes, cannot be turned back, and those who worked will not be deferred so that they may resume their work. Rather, the deeds have been concluded, and nothing remains but the recompense of the doers. {On that Day they will be divided}; that is, they will separate from one another on that Day, and they will depart in scattered, differing groups, so that their deeds may be shown to them.

{44–45} {Whoever disbelieves}: among them, {his disbelief will be upon him}: he will be punished for it himself, "no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another." {And whoever does righteous deeds}: of the rights that are due to Allah and those due to the servants, both obligatory and recommended, {it is for their own selves}: not for anyone else; {they prepare}; that is, they make ready, and for their own selves they build up their hereafter and prepare themselves to attain its abodes and lofty chambers. Moreover, their reward is not confined to their deeds; rather, Allah recompenses them from His abundant bounty and His limitless generosity with what their deeds could never reach. This is because He loves them, and when Allah loves a servant, He pours goodness upon him abundantly, bestows on him splendid gifts, and blesses him with outward and inward favours. This is in contrast to the disbelievers: when Allah has hated and detested them, He punishes and torments them, and does not increase them as He increased those before them. Therefore He said: {Indeed, He does not love the disbelievers}.

Therefore He said: {And although they were, before it was sent down upon them, already in despair (mublisin)}; that is, despairing and hopeless because its time of arrival had been delayed. So when it descended in that condition, it had a great effect upon them, and joy and rejoicing.

{50} {So look at the effects of Allah's mercy, how He gives life to the earth after its death}: so it stirred, swelled, and brought forth every lovely pair. {Indeed, that} (that which gave life to the earth after its death) {is the One who gives life to the dead, and He is over all things competent}: His power, may He be exalted, is not frustrated by anything, even if it is beyond the measure of His creation, subtle to their understanding, and their minds are bewildered by it.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 30, verses 51–53:

{51} He, may He be exalted, informs us about the state of creation: that despite these blessings upon them, in bringing the earth to life after its death and spreading His mercy, [they remain as they are]. If We were to send against this vegetation that grew from the rain, and against their crops, a wind that is harmful and destructive or diminishing, {and they see it turned yellow}: it has already begun to perish, {they would surely continue to disbelieve after it}: they forget the blessings of the past and hasten to disbelief! Such people are not benefited by admonition or warning.

{52} {Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear, nor can you make the deaf hear the call} {when they turn away, retreating}: and how much more so. For the barriers are firmly established in them against submission and beneficial hearing, just as the barriers mentioned above are firmly established against hearing a physical sound.

{53} {Nor can you guide the blind out of their misguidance}: because they do not accept sight due to their blindness; there is no receptiveness in them to it. {You can only make hear those who believe in Our signs, so they are Muslims}: these are the ones in whom the hearing of guidance is beneficial: those who believe in Our signs with their hearts, who submit to Our commands, who are Muslims to Us; for with them is the strong motive for accepting advice and admonitions, namely their readiness to believe in every sign of Allah, and their readiness to carry out what they are able to do of Allah's commands and prohibitions.

﴿He creates what He wills﴾: according to His wisdom. Among His wisdom is that He shows the servant his weakness, that his strength is enclosed between two weaknesses, that he has nothing of himself except deficiency, and that were it not for Allah's strengthening him, he would not have reached strength and capability. And had his strength continued to increase, he would have transgressed, oppressed and become insolent. And so that the servants may know the perfection of Allah's power, which never ceases to continue: He creates things by it, and manages affairs by it, and no fatigue, weakness or deficiency ever reaches it in any way whatsoever.

The commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 30, verses 55–57:

{55} He, exalted is He, informs about the Day of Resurrection and the swiftness of its coming, and that when the Hour is established, "the criminals" will swear by God that they "remained" in the world "only an hour." This is an excuse on their part, perhaps the excuse will benefit them, and a belittling of the duration of the worldly life. Since their statement was a lie with no reality to it, He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Thus were they deluded﴾; that is, they continued, while in the world, to be turned away from the realities (yu'fakun), and they habitually persisted in falsehood (ya'tafikun al-kadhib). In the world they denied the truth that the messengers had brought, and in the Hereafter they denied an evident matter, namely their long stay in the world. This is their ugly character, and a servant is resurrected upon what he died upon.

{56} ﴿And those who were given knowledge and faith﴾; that is, God bestowed these two upon them, and they became attributes of theirs: knowledge of the truth and faith, which necessarily entails preferring the truth. When they are people who know the truth and prefer it, it follows that their speech conforms to reality and suits their circumstances. Therefore they spoke the truth: ﴿Indeed you remained within the Book of God﴾; that is, within His decree and His destiny, which God wrote for you, and within His judgment, ﴿until the Day of Resurrection﴾; that is, you were given a lifespan in which the one who remembers could remember, the one who reflects could reflect, and the one who takes heed could take heed, until the Resurrection came and you reached this state. ﴿So this is the Day of Resurrection, but you were not knowing﴾; therefore you denied it in the world, and you denied your sojourn in the world, a time in which you could have been enabled to turn back in repentance. Ignorance remained your emblem, and its effects of denial and loss your shroud.

{57} ﴿So on that Day, the excuse of those who wronged will not benefit them﴾; if they deny, and claim that the proof was not established against them, or that they were not enabled to believe, their lie will be exposed by the testimony of the people of knowledge and faith, and by the testimony of their skins, hands and feet. And if they seek to be granted an excuse, and claim that they would return and not return to what they were forbidden, they will not be enabled, for the time of excuse has passed, so their excuse is not accepted. ﴿Nor will they be asked to make amends﴾; that is, their reproach will not be removed and reproof will not be lifted from them.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 30, verses 58–60:

{58 ـ 59} That is: ﴿And We have certainly set forth﴾, by virtue of Our care, Our mercy, Our kindness, and Our good instruction, ﴿for the people in this Qur'an every kind of example﴾, through which the realities become clear, matters are known, and the proof is made complete. This is general to the parables that God strikes to bring intelligible matters close to the perceptible, and to the reports of what will happen, making its reality so manifest that it is as if it had already occurred. Among them, in this passage, is God's mention of what will happen on the Day of Resurrection, the condition of the criminals therein, the intensity of their regret, and that no excuse or reproach will be accepted from them. But the wrongdoing disbelievers refused, except to oppose the manifest truth. For this reason He says: ﴿And if you were to bring them a sign﴾; that is, any sign that proves the truth of what you have brought, ﴿those who disbelieved would certainly say, "You are only nullifiers"﴾; that is, they said to the truth that it is falsehood. This is from their disbelief, their audacity, the sealing of God upon their hearts, and their extreme ignorance. For this reason He says: ﴿Thus does God seal the hearts of those who do not know﴾, so that no good enters them, and they do not perceive things as they truly are, but rather they see the truth as falsehood and falsehood as truth.

{60} ﴿So be patient﴾ in what you have been commanded and in calling them to God, even if you see aversion from them; let that not turn you away. ﴿Indeed, the promise of God is true﴾; that is, there is no doubt in it. This is something that helps one be patient, for when the servant knows that his deed is not lost, but that he will find it complete, what he encounters of hardships becomes easy for him, every difficulty is made easy for him, and every great deed seems small to him. ﴿And let not those who have no certainty make you unsteady﴾; that is, their faith has weakened and their certainty has diminished, so their forbearance has become light and their patience has become scant. So beware lest these people make you unsteady, and be wary of them; for if you do not keep them in mind and guard against them, they will make you light and lead you to fail to remain firm in the commands and prohibitions. The self assists them in this and seeks imitation and conformity. This shows that every believer who is certain and sound of intellect finds patience easy, while everyone of weak certainty is weak and light in intellect: the first is like the kernel, and the other like the husks. And God is the One whose help is sought.
